Title card 'COMMON MISTAKES - SHORT CIRCUIT'.

mistake: An extra red wire runs straight up from the red jumper's row (about row 8) to about row 18, bypassing the LED and resistor and shorting the circuit; the LED is dark.
why: A second, vertical red wire sits in the left terminal strip beside the resistor while the battery is connected and the LED is unlit, right after the 'short circuit' title.

mistake: An extra red wire goes diagonally from the positive red-jumper row (about row 8) to the LED/black-jumper side (about row 16), so current bypasses the LED and the circuit is shorted; the LED is dark.
why: Pliers point at the extra diagonal red wire; LED unlit with battery connected.

mistake: The extra diagonal red wire still connects the positive red-jumper row (about row 8) to the LED/ground side (about row 16), shorting past the LED and resistor; the LED stays dark.
why: Diagonal red wire still on the board, battery connected, LED unlit.

mistake: Battery snap is on the 9V battery while its bare red and black leads hang loose off the board, tips close together, risking a direct short if they touch.
why: Hands hold the snapped-on battery's stripped leads near each other with no breadboard in use.

mistake: Battery snap is attached to the battery with the bare red and black lead ends lying loose and close together on the table, risking a battery short.
why: Snapped-on 9V battery with stripped leads a few millimetres apart, not in any rail.
